newsitem.title: UK: Early LME trade routine, copper rallies strongly.
newsitem.headline: Early LME trade routine, copper rallies strongly.

text.p: Trading in base metals remained was during pre-market London Metal Exchange (LME) trading on Friday, with the only notable mover being the copper contract which rallied sharply after dipping on a LME stocks rise.
Three months delivery copper was last at $2,361, the morning's high and $33 up on Thursday's kerb close.
The price had been as low as $2,334 after a near 2,000 tonnes stocks rise after forecasts of a fall in of between 1,000 and 5,000 tonnes.
"We saw the obvious reaction in the market," one trader said referring to the inventory rise.
But markets were thin and early business in all base metals remained slow.
Copper was expected to try to consolidate after its recent gains, which could mean fluctuations of around $40.
Copper's cash to three months copper spread was quoted at little changed levels of around a $80 backwardation.

Aluminium was underpinned by a stocks fall of 2,400 tonnes but was meeting stiff resistance and selling on probes towards $1,615. Traders said the market had to break above these levels to spark further gains towards $1,650.
Nickel was last at $7,860, up $10, and paying little attention to a stocks rise.
Zinc traded at $1,212 versus a $1,216 close on Thursday.
Tin was slightly lower after a stocks rise and was quoted at $6,000/10, compared with $6,020, and alloy was little moved at $1,535.
